A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work despite renaming REPOA to XENON and changing the title. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original MineRL and MC-TextWorld experiments, including dependency-learning curves, task success rates, ablations, and appendix error analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds Mineflayer, TextWorld Cooking, robustness, scalability, and controller-comparison results.

M1.justification: The principal dependency-revision, action-memory, DEX, and CRe procedures survive the renaming. The reported revision trigger changes from aggregate net failures reaching d0 to all actions being classified invalid (Algorithms 1). Appendix A also adapts ADG to single-precondition cooking tasks. These are localized procedural changes.

E1.justification: v2 adds Mineflayer and the household TextWorld Cooking domain. Minecraft coverage also expands through additional leather, paper, flint, and other goal items, unmodified MineRL resource conditions, larger action spaces, and environments whose rules change during learning. The original 67-goal coverage is retained.

E2.justification: v2 adds an SC agent correcting both dependencies and actions to the dependency-learning comparisons; this is broader than v1's dependency-only self-correction ablation. Appendix K additionally evaluates DEPS† and OracleActionPlanner in controller comparisons, and Random+FAM, UCB, and an LLM without memory in action-selection experiments.

E3.justification: The reported MC-TextWorld horizon changes from 2,000 to 3,000 steps, and fixed rule modifications become graded randomized requirement/action perturbations, including combined perturbations. New protocols compare 4B/7B planners, one/three initial plans, and different action-set sizes. Cooking uses 50-step episodes with ingredients and tools supplied; dynamic-rule tests notify agents which items changed.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands mechanism testing through separated dependency/action-correction ablations, hyperparameter sensitivity, controller and oracle-planner controls, dynamic-rule recovery, misleading external knowledge, goal/action scalability, and weaker-planner/initial-knowledge tests (Sections 5.5–5.6 and K.2–K.11). The earlier initial-graph and planning-error analyses are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: v1 reports MC-TextWorld means and standard deviations over 20 episodes; v2 specifies 15 runs and omission of negligible standard deviations. New experiments disclose three independent 100-episode cooking runs and 20 runs per goal for action selection. These refine repetition and uncertainty reporting without introducing a substantially different statistical framework.

E6.justification: Substantial new results include Mineflayer EGA near 0.9, cooking success rates of 1.00 versus SC's 0.75 and DECKARD's 0.09, and zero Diamond/Gold success under standard MineRL conditions (Table 14). Revised ablations and perturbation settings add further results. The original aggregate and per-goal MineRL scores remain unchanged after renaming, including overall learned/oracle success rates of 0.54/0.79.

T1.justification: The DAG formulation, requirement-set definitions, Ntrue objective in Equation 1, and DEX selection mathematics are retained. The added cycle-handling discussion explains implementation; it does not introduce a new formal theoretical result, proof, or substantive derivation.

C1.justification: The central claims of robust experience-based planning and a 7B-model advantage remain. v2 narrows the 'from scratch' framing toward correcting flawed priors under binary feedback, makes superiority to LLM self-correction an explicit headline claim, and no longer presents DEX/sample efficiency as a principal contribution.

C2.justification: v2 replaces v1's brief Redstone explanation involving item-name ambiguity with a detailed account of missing analogous experience and controller resource limits. Standard-MineRL controls sharpen applicability boundaries. It also qualifies action correction's usefulness without accurate dependencies and explains the increasing exploration cost of larger action spaces, substantially expanding interpretation beyond v1.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-access link, SC prompts, cycle-prevention instructions, environment versions/API mappings, and detailed perturbation and additional-goal specifications. Hardware and compute disclosures are retained. Documentation has drawbacks: Table 15 drops earlier error-analysis episode totals; x0 is 2 in the main text but -2 in Table 7; Algorithm 3 omits the counter increment described in prose.

R1.justification: v2 substantially develops positioning against LLM self-correction, adding literature including Reflexion, CRITIC, and self-verification studies in Section 2.2. Much of v1's broader environmental-knowledge-learning discussion is replaced, while additional long-context and small-model literature supports the revised positioning. This exceeds merely moving related work into the main text.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method exposition, results discussion, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. REPOA/ADL/FFOM become XENON/ADG/FAM, related work moves into the main text, and the overall algorithm and DEX move into appendices. The appendix organization is extensively rebuilt.

P2.justification: v2 adds failure-example, agent-overview, knowledge-correction, and perturbation diagrams, alongside numerous new experimental plots and tables. Existing displays are also reorganized: MineRL learning is paired with Mineflayer, the main success-rate table gains a planner-LLM column, and component ablations are restructured. These are substantial visual changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: v2 materially strengthens evidence for why the method works and where it fails. Self-correction comparisons, separated mechanism ablations, sensitivity tests, and standard-MineRL/oracle-planner controls address important gaps in v1's validation and controller-limit analysis. Mineflayer and cooking broaden supporting evidence without relying on improved retained benchmark scores. Threshold, pseudocode, and some table inconsistencies limit reproducibility, but the stronger experimental controls and clearer applicability boundaries provide a substantial net improvement.
